title: Parallel Processing (Batching)
hook: Checking email between every task is quietly eating your whole afternoon.
statement: Group similar tasks together so you're not constantly switching gears.
explainer: Every switch costs more than the seconds it takes to open a tab. Your focus needs minutes to fully come back, and that cost never shows up on a spreadsheet.
sop: List your task types: email, content, calls, admin, creative.
Give each type its own block on your calendar.
Count how many Switches your current day forces.
Turn off notifications for everything but the current batch.
Protect the blocks for 2 weeks before judging.
equation_example: 15 Switches a day: 1 ÷ 15 = about 0.067. Cut to 3 Switches: 1 ÷ 3 = about 0.33. That's five times more efficient. Fewer switches means a higher score. More means more of your day lost to refocusing.
question: Pick one scattered task type and write when you'll batch it this week.
closing_statement: Every switch charges a hidden refocusing fee.
